discovery: Prediction and experimental demonstration of anyonic (fractional) exchange statistics in the fractional quantum Hall effect

nominees.name: Gwendal Fève
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire de Physique de l'École Normale Supérieure, Paris, France

motivation: Quantum mechanics in two dimensions allows particles that are neither bosons nor fermions. For decades these anyons stayed a theoretical idea. Halperin showed that fractional quantum Hall quasiparticles must obey fractional exchange statistics, and he laid the hierarchy and edge-state framework that made the statistics measurable. In 2020 two complementary experiments confirmed it directly. Fève and collaborators built an anyon collider, in which current cross-correlations revealed the braiding phase of Laughlin quasiparticles at filling 1/3. Manfra's group engineered ultra-high-mobility GaAs heterostructures and Fabry-Pérot interferometers and observed discrete phase slips that match the predicted anyonic braiding phase. Together these results establish a third kind of quantum statistics in nature, a conceptual extension of the spin-statistics picture taught to every physics student. They also open the way to non-Abelian anyons and topologically protected quantum computation.
